the waterproofing lipoidal barrier of the cuticle is a composite structure, and that its properties are determined by a combination of the physical characteristics of the lipids, the geometry of their arrangement, and the nature of the underlying cuticular structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the waterproofing lipoidal layer of the cuticle is the most important factor in controlling the transpiration of the insect.
the waterproofing lipoidal layer is not a continuous film of wax, but a mosaic of wax and other lipids.

the waterproofing of the insect cuticle is due to a complex structure, which consists of the epicuticle, a layer of lipids that are probably secreted by the epidermis, the epicuticular canals that penetrate the outer epicuticular layer, and the pore canals, which extend from the surface through the cuticle to the tracheae.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the insect cuticle is not a single barrier, but is composed of several barriers, each with its own permeability characteristics and its own temperature dependence of permeability.
the waterproofing layer is a complex structure that is not simply a single layer of lipids.
the insect cuticle is a very dynamic structure.
